title: Physicists Caged a Single Antimatter Particle for Months
title_options: Physicists Caged a Single Antimatter Particle for Months
Before This Positron, There Was Priscilla (1984)
The Antimatter Cage Began as a Vacuum Gauge
first_frame_headline: It vanishes if it touches anything.

claim_stamp.note: Peer-reviewed device paper (Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 173001, 21 Oct 2026). The positron-vs-electron comparison is not measured yet.

sources_on_screen: Myers et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 173001 (2026)

beats.say: Antimatter vanishes the moment it touches anything. Yet in October twenty twenty-six, physicists reported holding one anti-electron, a positron, for months.
beats.vis: FROM FRAME 0 the hook scene stands on the desk (STORY_FORMAT identity rule): a single glowing dot floats in empty dark space inside a drawn glass-and-steel trap and never touches the edges (C010). A hand-drawn calendar shows 'OCT 2026' and a counter that keeps ticking 'MONTHS'. First-frame headline: 'It vanishes if it touches anything.' ARTISTIC: the dot's look.
beats.src_line: Myers et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 173001 (2026)

beats.say: So they built a container with no walls. Magnetic and electric fields hold it in the middle, touching nothing.
beats.vis: Cutaway of the trap: field lines as ribbons, end caps and ring as simple discs, the dot bobbing along the axis and turning back before each cap (Dehmelt's Fig. 1 shape). Quote card, attributed: 'a container without walls' (Gabrielse).

beats.say: One ancestor was a vacuum gauge. In nineteen thirty-six, Frans Penning used a magnet to measure almost-empty air.
beats.vis: Signpost card '1936'. Caption 'one ancestor of the trap (Dehmelt's own account: C052, C064)'. A glass discharge tube between magnet poles (shape of Fig. 1 of US 2,197,079: two parallel plates and a frame anode in a glass bulb); electrons curl in long loops instead of the straight shortcut. ARTISTIC: the lab. No portrait of Penning (none sourced).

beats.say: Decades later, Dehmelt wrote that he wondered how to hold one electron still, then built a trap from Penning's gauge, and named it after him.
beats.vis: Signpost 'DECADES LATER · SEATTLE'. A blackboard with a single chalk dot and the words 'Here is an electron...' on a quote card (Dehmelt's recollection of his teacher, C051). The dot slides off the board into the trap drawing from b02; text 'Penning trap'. ARTISTIC: classroom, no face for the teacher. Voice attributes everything to 'Dehmelt wrote' (rule 10.3: his own account, no independent record of the naming).
beats.src_line: Dehmelt, Physica Scripta T22 (1988); Am. J. Phys. 58 (1990)

beats.say: But holding one for months is not a first. Dehmelt's lab announced a positron named Priscilla, held in their trap for three months.
beats.vis: THE HOLD (peak). Signpost card 'SEATTLE · SEP 15, 1984'. The b01 dot returns wearing a small pet-style name tag 'PRISCILLA' and a '3 MONTHS' counter; let the tag sit for about 1 s. The viewer sees the b01 picture again, 42 years apart (plant and payoff, C11). On-screen quote cards, in this order, both attributed to Dehmelt's 1988 paper (not voiced): (1) the lab's announcement, 'Here, right now, in the center of our Penning trap resides positron Priscilla ... executing simple spontaneous ballet routines for the last 3 months!' (C091); (2) during the b05 pause, '...she never had the chance of trading places with a passing twin.' (C092), with a twin dot drifting past the named dot. If the frame is crowded, cut card (2) first. ARTISTIC: the tag and the twin dot.

beats.say: So what is new? Gabrielse's team cooled theirs almost to absolute zero, and can nudge it up one tiny energy step at a time.
beats.vis: Energy ladder drawn as a short staircase: the dot on the bottom step, a microwave pulse lifts it one step, the staircase glows, then it falls back. Data label '0.3 K' on screen (C004, not spoken). Small tag: 'before: classical motion' (C099).
beats.src_line: Myers et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 173001 (2026)

beats.say: The paper is published. The big test, matching it against an electron, is not done.
beats.vis: Claim stamp slams in (stamp SFX): 'PUBLISHED'. Beside it the tag 'positron vs electron: not measured yet' (C015). The other rungs (REPEATED, ON SALE) stay unlit.
beats.src_line: Myers et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 173001 (2026)

beats.say: One particle, caged for months. Priscilla had a name. What would you call this one?
beats.vis: The hook dot floats in the trap as in b01, now with an empty name tag. The final scene shrinks into the drawer and it shuts (DeskShrink + DeskClose), looping to frame 0. ARTISTIC: the blank tag.

review.note: Story gate S13: one pass with the Bhagyaraj method and one with the Nolan method (Mode B). Facts locked to ledger IDs; no fact was added. Changes made are listed under 'applied'.

bhagyaraj.question: If one positron was already held for months in 1984, what did 2026 add?
plants_and_payoffs: b01 floating dot + 'months' counter -> b05 same picture 42 years earlier
b01 'touches anything and vanishes' -> b05 twin dot drifts past and Priscilla stays herself (on screen, C092)
b05 name tag 'PRISCILLA' -> b08 blank tag and the viewer's question
bhagyaraj.heart: A positron with a pet name; Dehmelt's 'ballet routines' announcement (C091) carries the humour and is on screen at no word cost.
bhagyaraj.weakest: Penning and Dehmelt are voices without faces (no portraits are sourced). The human note is Dehmelt's wondering (C051) and Priscilla's name.

nolan.theme: What is new is control, not endurance.
nolan.shape: Hairpin: 2026 dot (b01) -> 1936 gauge -> 1950s trap -> 1984 dot (b05, the same picture) -> 2026 steps (b06) -> blank tag (b08, rhymes with b01).

pledge_turn_prestige.pledge: b01-b02: one particle held for months in a container with no walls
pledge_turn_prestige.turn: b05: it was already done in 1984
pledge_turn_prestige.prestige: b06-b08: the new part is one-quantum control, and the real test is still ahead

nolan.fair_play: The twist is planted in b01 ('reported', 'for months'), b02 (the trap) and b04 (Dehmelt's trap decades earlier); a viewer can replay it and see the clue.
nolan.loop: b08 ends on the b01 image and re-uses its line 'caged for months'. The desk shrinks and shuts into frame 0.
nolan.strands: One strand at a time (1936 -> 1959 -> 1984 -> 2026); no cross-cutting, per AK's followability guard.

b05: 'But this is not a first' -> 'But holding one for months is not a first' (the old line did not say what was not a first).
b05 picture: added the 'ballet routines' announcement card (C091) before the twin card (C092); neither is voiced.
